title: PathWeaver: A High-Throughput Multi-GPU System for Graph-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
problem: Existing multi-GPU ANNS solutions overlook scalability and use naive dataset partitioning that treats additional GPUs merely as memory extensions. Independent searching on each GPU partition results in redundant search iterations and poor multi-GPU utilization.
motivation: Graph-based ANNS is critical for recommendation systems, NLP, and computer vision applications, and efficient multi-GPU scaling is essential as datasets grow.
method: PathWeaver introduces three coordinated techniques: (1) pipelining-based path extension that leverages GPU-to-GPU communication to reduce redundant search iterations, (2) ghost staging that identifies optimal query starting points using representative datasets, and (3) direction-guided selection that filters irrelevant points early to minimize memory accesses and distance computations.
key_novelty: Pipelining-based path extension mechanism that leverages GPU-to-GPU communication to eliminate redundant search iterations in multi-GPU ANNS systems.
contributions: Pipelining-based path extension enabling efficient GPU-aware multi-GPU coordination
Ghost staging technique for optimal query starting point identification
Direction-guided selection for early filtering of irrelevant data points
Achieves 3.24x geomean speedup and up to 5.30x speedup on 95% recall over prior approaches
